newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bosnian Serb gets 20 years in prison for warcrimes.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb gets 20 years in prison for warcrimes.

text.p: The U.N. tribunal for the former Yugoslavia on Monday sentenced Bosnian Serb Dusan Tadic to 20 years in prison for war crimes and crimes against humanity.
The sentence followed a tribunal decision on May 7 which found Tadic guilty of taking part in a Serb ethnic cleansing campaign against Bosnian Moslems in the early stages of Bosnia's war in 1992.

During a seven-months trial last year, prosecutors charged that Tadic, 41, rounded up former Moslem neighbours in the Prijedor region of northwest Bosnia, then tortured, raped and killed them in Serb-run detention camps.

A panel of three judges convicted him on 11 counts of persecution and beatings, but acquitted him on nine counts of murder and declared 11 charges inapplicable. He was also found guilty of complicity in the killing of two policemen.
Tadic has always denied the charges, claiming he was a victim of the Moslems' desire to find a scapegoat for their suffering at the hands of the Serbs.
His lawyers have lodged an appeal against the guilty verdict.
